question.text: Which section of the Income Tax Act provides for the taxation of long-term capital gains on equity-oriented mutual funds?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the Income Tax Act, 1961, Section 112A is the charging section for long-term capital gains on equity-oriented mutual funds (and listed equity shares) on which Securities Transaction Tax has been paid. Section 111A correspondingly charges short-term capital gains on the same class of assets, while Section 112 deals with LTCG on other capital assets, and Section 10(23D) provides an exemption to the mutual fund scheme's own income. The Trap: Section 111A and Section 112A are easily confused — 111A applies to short-term equity, 112A applies to long-term equity. Section 112 (without 'A') applies to non-equity LTCG, and Section 10(23D) is a scheme-level exemption, not a charging provision for unit-holder gains. Note: The cited NISM Series V-A Mutual Fund Distributors workbook supports the LTCG taxability rules and the Rs.1.25 lakh exemption for equity-oriented MF LTCG, but the explicit section number 'Section 112A' was not located in the pages reviewed. The framing above reflects current Income Tax Act statutory references rather than a direct workbook citation.
